pos.personaBrief: Total Football's major component was the use of space and the need to constantly create it, with pressing to win the ball back (verified, Ajax era); Michels's teams wanted to control games with the ball rather than cede it to counter.

pro.personaBrief: No verified evidence on progression (gap axis); from general knowledge Michels's Ajax combined short build-up through a sweeper-keeper and defenders with fast, forward-minded attacking, consistent with the verified space-creating, pressing style.

est.personaBrief: The fluid 4-3-3 had players 'regularly switching positions to ensure that the tactical roles in the team were consistently filled' (verified): roles stay defined but players rotate, spread out to create space, with the centre-forward (Cruyff) dropping in.

lar.personaBrief: No verified evidence on width (gap axis); from general knowledge the 4-3-3 relied on genuine wingers (Keizer, Swart, Rep, Rensenbrink) to stretch the pitch, which fits the verified emphasis on creating space.

blo.personaBrief: The system used the offside trap and pressing 'to win back the ball' (verified, Ajax era), meaning a high line and aggressive pressure far from goal.

mar.personaBrief: An offside trap and collective pressing (verified) require defenders who hold a line and squeeze space rather than follow individual opponents, so Michels's defending was zonal and collective.

pla.personaBrief: No verified evidence on game plan (gap axis); from general knowledge Michels imposed Total Football as a fixed model at Ajax, Barcelona and the Netherlands, consistent with the verified system of rotation, pressing and offside trap.

res.personaBrief: No verified evidence on purpose (gap axis); from general knowledge Michels saw football as 'war' and was driven to win, yet his attacking style and the remembered 1974 side show he never played to protect a result.

sis.personaBrief: No verified evidence on system versus talent (gap axis); from general knowledge Michels's collective of interchanging roles (verified rotation) put the system first and demanded defensive work from all, though Cruyff had licence to roam.

jog.personaBrief: No verified evidence on player type (gap axis); from general knowledge Michels demanded both technique and intense fitness, since constant pressing and rotation (verified) require every player to run and be good on the ball.

bas.personaBrief: No verified evidence on squad building (gap axis); from general knowledge Michels built Ajax's European Cup side around young academy players such as Cruyff, Keizer and Swart, though at Barcelona he relied on signings.

lid.personaBrief: No verified evidence on leadership (gap axis); from general knowledge Michels was 'The General', a strict disciplinarian who imposed hard training and rules on the whole squad.
